messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT — streaming.p99(us-west-2) spiked above SLO (currently 11.8s) at 2026-07-21T01:00:10Z. page: #eng-oncall. triggered runbook: contbatch-tail-investigation.

incidents-bot: paging sara_oncall, mike_sre, juan_reliability. impact: ~5% of streaming requests > timeout (10s).

sara_oncall: I'm here, acknowledging. grabbing initial graphs from dashboard now.

sara_oncall: quick note — this looks like continuous-batching path only, streaming routes. non-streaming gen routes okay.

mike_sre: getting scheduler metrics. seeing average batch_size jump to ~42 with tail batches at 128. CPU/GPU utilization normal, but KV cache miss rate rising. link: https://dash.internal/r/streaming/scheduler

juan_reliability: mixed-seqlen amplification possibility — if short chats get batched with very long responses we pay padding cost and KV eviction churn. saw similar in canary last quarter.

ashley_prodeng: alex_support — any customer reports?

alex_support: yes, a couple of premium tenants hit streaming timeouts, ticket IDs CS-4981, CS-4983. Both observed repeated stalls in the stream (clients got 504 after stall). customers notified.

sara_oncall: initial hypothesis: continuous batching scheduler is grouping heterogeneous seq lengths, creating oversized batches -> longer per-request latency plus KV eviction -> streaming stalls.

mike_sre: corroborating. scheduler fairness skew metrics show small requests getting starved behind a few huge sequences; p95 impacted too.

juan_reliability: propose immediate live mitigations: 1) disable contbatch for streaming routes, 2) cap max_batch_size to 8 for streaming, 3) add route-level seq-length cap/soft-drop for requests > 30k tokens, 4) route long sequences to isolated pool. can do 1+2 quickly.

sara_oncall: agreed. plan: apply mitigations in this order: A) toggle contbatch off -> measure p99. B) if not enough, reduce max_batch_size -> measure. C) follow with routing rules. D) open postmortem and long-term scheduler fix.

mike_sre: preparing commands. will push small config change to control-plane.

mike_sre: deploy-bot: run playbook contbatch-disable-streaming in us-west-2

deploy-bot: playbook accepted, running change in 3 mins. will post rollout ID.

mike_sre: rollout id: r-20260721-001. command I ran:
```
redwoodctl routes update --region us-west-2 --route streaming --set continuous_batching=false --reason "live mitigation: contbatch p99 spike"
```

mike_sre: also lowering max batch size for streaming route:
```
redwoodctl routes update --region us-west-2 --route streaming --set max_batch_size=8
```

mike_sre: changes applied to 70% of nodes, rolling. watching metrics.

incidents-bot: NOTE — change r-20260721-001 detected in control plane. Health checks will block if error rate > 1%.

sara_oncall: tracing a few live traces. before mitigation I see batch durations stretched to 6-12s. after partial rollout some traces show single-request fast path 120-200ms.

juan_reliability: good sign. also recommend temporary KV-cache size bump on streaming workers to reduce eviction while we stabilize. low risk.

mike_sre: issuing KV bump via infra task:
```
infractl config set --pool streaming-usw2 --kv_cache_slots=4096
```

mike_sre: KV bump applied.

ashley_prodeng: customer comms: updating the two affected customers with ETA for full restoration.

alex_support: noted. customers asked for workaround: prefer fallbacks to non-streaming route for heavy requests — routing option sent.

incidents-bot: Metrics update at +6m: p99 dropped from 11.8s -> 2.1s; p95 back under SLO. error rate falling to baseline.

sara_oncall: looks like mitigations worked. recommend keep contbatch disabled for streaming until postmortem and scheduler fairness fix.

juan_reliability: for postmortem action items: - implement seqlen-aware batching (prefer grouping similar seqlen), - preemptive batch-shedding for mixed batches, - isolated queue for requests with declared "long" token hint, - overload routing to fall back to a lower-latency variant.

mike_sre: I'll open infra tasks for seqlen-aware scheduler and a small experiment to prioritize small-slow fairness.

ashley_prodeng: also add an Optimize recommendation: suggest customer-side token limit and chunking guidance to reduce long-stream mixes.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated. status: partial_routing_mitigated -> monitoring. escalation: none. assigning follow-ups: mike_sre (scheduler fix task), juan_reliability (postmortem lead), sara_oncall (verify long-tail tests).

sara_oncall: closing here for on-call shift handover. will document timeline in incident tracker. if anyone sees regressions ping this thread.

mike_sre: noted. I'll attach sample spans and scheduler logs to the ticket.

juan_reliability: creating postmortem draft now. initial summary will mention contbatch padding amplification due to mixed sequence lengths and scheduler fairness.

alex_support: tickets updated and customers looped in. CC: account managers.

deploy-bot: rollout r-20260721-001 completed -> 100% nodes. no blocked health checks.

incidents-bot: final metrics at +18m: p99 = 1.9s, p95 = 210ms, error rate normalized. monitoring -> continue 2h.

sara_oncall: thanks team. handing off to next oncall.

mike_sre: one more thing — add a synthetic test that mixes short and very long seq to catch padding amplification in CI. I'll add to perf suite.
